content: The inhibition of gastrointestinal (GI) absorption applies exclusively to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darifenacin reduces the effects of pantoprazole through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Theoretical considerations suggest that the effectiveness of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) may be diminished when co-administered with other antisecretory agents. Devil's claw decreases the effects of pantoprazole via pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Dexamethasone reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. The combination of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF with pantoprazole affects hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Based on drug interaction studies with the components of Stribild, no clinically significant interactions have been observed or are expected when co-administered with PPIs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Eslcarbazepine acetate reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor for GI symptoms, as the net effect on PPI action remains unclear due to opposing CYP450 actions. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Pantoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferric carboxymaltose by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Fosphenytoin reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, as well as hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Levo-ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism and hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Pantoprazole reduces the levels of levothyroxine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction, and its clinical significance is unknown. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of liothyronine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction, and its clinical significance is unknown. Pantoprazole reduces the levels of liotrix by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction, and its clinical significance is unknown. Pantoprazole reduces the levels of methamphetamine by decreasing the time to maximum concentration (Tmax) of amphetamine. Monitor patients for changes in clinical effects and adjust therapy based on clinical response. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Modafinil increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The net effect on pantoprazole actions is unclear due to opposing effects of CYP450 enzymes. Monitor closely. Oxcarbazepine reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The net effect on pantoprazole actions is unclear due to opposing effects of CYP450 enzymes. Monitor closely. Pentobarbital reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of phytoestrogens by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Pantoprazole reduces the levels of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of thyroid desiccated by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction, and its clinical significance is unknown. Acalabrutinib increases the levels of pantoprazole through an unspecified mechanism. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH. Acalabrutinib solubility decreases with increasing gastric pH. Due to the long-lasting effect of PPIs, separating doses may not eliminate the interaction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of alpelisib through an unspecified mechanism. Co-administration of alpelisib (a BCRP substrate) with a BCRP inhibitor may increase alpelisib concentration, raising the risk of toxicities. If unable to avoid or substitute alternative drugs, closely monitor for increased adverse reactions. Amobarbital reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ampicillin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by increasing elimination and by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration of apalutamide, a strong CYP2C19 inducer, with drugs that are CYP2C19 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. Avoid or substitute another drug when possible. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if co-administration is necessary. Pantoprazole reduces the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations of atazanavir when co-administered with PPIs. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. For treatment-naive patients, the PPI dose should not exceed a dose comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken approximately 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir. Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of atogepant by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole reduces the levels or effects of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg orally twice daily when co-administered with PPIs. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole increases the levels of berotralstat through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor berotralstat (a BCRP substrate) for adverse effects when co-administered with a BCRP inhibitor. Blessed thistle reduces the effects of pantoprazole via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This is a theoretical interaction, and its clinical significance is unknown. Bortezomib reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of bosutinib by approximately 45% due to bosutinib's pH-dependent solubility. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause extended-release budesonide tablets to prematurely dissolve, potentially affecting release properties and absorption in the duodenum. Monitor closely. Butabarbital reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider reducing the dose of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates when co-administered with cannabidiol. Monitor closely. Cannabidiol increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole reduces the effects of capecitabine through an unknown mechanism. Retrospective data suggest that elevated gastric pH caused by PPI use may impair capecitabine tablet dissolution and/or reduce absorption. Monitor closely. Carbamazepine reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. Cenobamate increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider a dose reduction of CYP2C19 substrates when used concomitantly with cenobamate. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole reduces the levels or effects of ceritinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole increases the toxicity of cilostazol by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider decreasing the cilostazol dose, as moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase serum levels of 3,4-dehydrocilostazol (an active metabolite). Monitor closely. Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of clobazam by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Dosage adjustment may be required, as CYP2C19 inhibitors may result in increased exposure to N-desmethylclobazam (an active metabolite). Monitor closely. Pantoprazole reduces the effects of clopidogrel by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Clopidogrel efficacy may be reduced by drugs that inhibit CYP2C19. However, pantoprazole prescribing information states that co-administration with clopidogrel had no clinically important effect on exposure to clopidogrel's active metabolite, and no dose adjustment of clopidogrel is required. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may decrease the solubility of crizotinib and subsequently reduce its bioavailability. However, no formal studies have been conducted. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole decreases the levels of cyanocobalamin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole and cyclosporine may increase the toxicity of each other through an unspecified mechanism. Prolonged PPI use may cause hypomagnesemia, and the risk is further increased when used concomitantly with drugs that have the same effects. Monitor closely. Dabrafenib reduces the levels or effects of pantoprazole by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Pantoprazole reduces the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. Drugs that alter upper GI tract pH (e.g., PPIs, H2-blockers, antacids) may decrease dabrafenib solubility and reduce its bioavailability. Use an alternative if available. Monitor closely. Pantoprazole increases the levels or effects of dacomitinib through an unspecified mechanism. Concomitant use with a PPI decreases dacomitinib concentrations, which may reduce its efficacy. Avoid the use of PPIs with dacomitinib. As an alternative to PPIs, use locally-acting antacids or an H2-receptor antagonist. Administer at least 6 hours before or 10 hours after taking an H2-receptor antagonist. Monitor closely. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole through an unspecified mechanism. Danicopan increases plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates; consider dose reduction of BCRP substrates according to their prescribing information. Monitor closely. Darifenacin reduces the effects of pantoprazole through an unspecified mechanism. Theoretical considerations suggest that the effectiveness of PPIs may be diminished when co-administered with other antisecretory agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Darolutamide increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole through an unspecified mechanism. Darolutamide is a BCRP inhibitor. Avoid co-administration with BCRP inhibitors. If use is unavoidable, closely monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of BCRP substrate drugs. Monitor closely.
